text:
Shreya Patel: Quick sync — we got a few incoming customer asks and internal questions about the embeddings endpoint MVP. Main asks: support 4096-dim vectors, preserve input order + ids, and allow large client batching (they mentioned 10k items). What do we ship for MVP?

Alex Kim: 10k items at 4096 dims isn't realistic for hosted without chunking. Memory combo is brutal. We should set a hard request cap and do server-side sharding. Proposal: per-request max_items=2048 for 4096-dim model, 4096 max_items for 1024-dim model. Also expose a header X-Redwood-Batch-Parts when we split.

Derek Li: +1 on shard header. Runtime can transparently split into sub-batches of ~256-512 per GPU to keep latency SLOs. For Dedicated customers we can raise limits via config.

Maria Gomez: Customer-facing requirement: they need deterministic output ordering and an opaque id echoed back so they can map results. They also want minimal response size (no extra metadata per vector). Can we standardize response shape to: 

```
[ { "id": "<client-id>", "embedding": [0.001, ...] }, ... ]
```

and add an optional top-level "model" field?

Alex Kim: That shape is fine. We should include an optional meta object only when requested (e.g., include_probabilities=false by default). Keep default minimal.

Samir Rao: Model selection: recommend two variants for launch — embed-lite (1024 dims, faster) and embed-std (4096 dims). Map them to different performance profiles in Console and call them out in docs with expected tokens/s and cost multipliers.

Shreya Patel: Sounds reasonable. Need to capture launch criteria: 1) SDKs accept array + id echoing, 2) server-side sharding implemented + header, 3) docs + example contract, 4) internal perf benchmarks showing latency < 300ms p95 for 256-item 4096-dim requests on Dedicated baseline. Anyone add/remove?

Derek Li: Add: fallback policy — when out of capacity, auto-fallback to embed-lite and attach warning header X-Redwood-Fallback=model:embed-lite. Product must be okay with quality variance.

Maria Gomez: Also add: response ordering guarantee in SLA text — we promise preserve input order even when sharded (we'll reassemble). If fallback occurs we note it in response metadata.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: embeddings/sharder v1 -> staging at 2026-04-02T03:00:00Z :rocket:

Alex Kim: Quick API example to add to docs (minimal):

```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "embed-std-4096",
  "inputs": [ { "id": "u1", "text": "..." }, { "id": "u2", "text": "..." } ]
}

200 OK
[
  { "id": "u1", "embedding": [0.0001, ...] },
  { "id": "u2", "embedding": [0.0002, ...] }
]
```

Shreya Patel: Action items: @Alex update SDK PR with id echo + batch header, @Derek implement sharder and fallback header, @Maria draft the customer-facing contract paragraph and benchmark targets. I'll coordinate launch checklist.

Samir Rao: Can we add an opt-in query param `preserve_meta=true` that returns model name + shard info when customers want full traceability? Low overhead if optional.

Alex Kim: Good idea. We'll include query param and a `verbosity` param in SDKs.

Maria Gomez: I'll surface this in the next customer sync. If they insist on 10k raw items we'll present Dedicated upgrade path (configurable max_items).

Shreya Patel: Great — let's run with that for the MVP and reconvene after the staging deploy. :thumbsup:
